purpose: Report corruption, bribery, procurement fraud, diversion of public funds, money laundering, and abuse of office
Route petitions to the correct anti-corruption institution(s) and copy relevant watchdogs
Support evidence-based, non-defamatory reporting with clear timelines and documents

federal_ministry_of_justice.name: Federal Ministry of Justice
aliases: Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation

core_anti_corruption_agencies.name: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
focus: Financial crimes, fraud, cyber-enabled fraud, money laundering

contact.address: Plot 301/302, Institution and Research Cadastral District, Jabi, Abuja, Nigeria

core_anti_corruption_agencies.name: Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC)
aliases: Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission
focus: Bribery, abuse of office, corruption in public sector/service delivery

contact.address: 5th Floor, Federal Secretariat Complex Annex III, Shehu Shagari Way, Maitama, Abuja, Nigeria

procurement_audit_transparency.name: Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP)
focus: Procurement fraud red flags, bid rigging indicators (report with evidence)

watchdogs.name: Public Complaints Commission (PCC)
role: Maladministration and failure of MDAs to respond or act properly on complaints
Service failure, extortion in administrative processes, refusal to acknowledge complaints

watchdogs.name: National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
role: Where corruption allegations connect to rights violations (unlawful detention, torture to extort, etc.)

priority_logic: If the allegation is financial fraud / laundering / scam: EFCC first, copy FMOJ and PCC where maladministration exists.
If the allegation is bribery/abuse of office/service delivery corruption in MDAs: ICPC first, copy PCC.
If it is assets declaration or conflict-of-interest of a public officer: CCB first (and copy ICPC where needed).
If it is procurement inflation / contract splitting / bid rigging: BPP first (copy ICPC/EFCC depending on evidence).

complaint_and_escalation_flow.step_1: Write a factual petition: who/what/when/where/how; attach evidence; avoid insults/defamation.
complaint_and_escalation_flow.step_2: Send to the primary agency based on allegation type (EFCC/ICPC/CCB/BPP).
complaint_and_escalation_flow.step_3: Copy PCC where there is maladministration (refusal to respond, extortion, abuse of process, cover-up).
complaint_and_escalation_flow.step_4: If threats/retaliation occur, document it and add NHRC to protect rights and safety.

evidence_checklist: Full names and roles of persons involved (or titles if names unknown)
Project/contract title and award details (where applicable)
Amounts, account details, payment references (if available)
Screenshots, emails, WhatsApp chats (exported), call logs (where lawful)
